SystemSketch · deep research dictionary · 04 September 2026

LabVIEW, Unreal Blueprint & Simulink
Vocabulary and UI Controls Gap Analysis

A table-like evidence dictionary: mature visual-programming tools as reading-grammar precedent, never as a template for a second Python authoring language.

How to read a useful row

Useful entries are deliberately in this order: plain-language description, actual vendor documentation screenshots side by side, then an original SystemSketch proposal drawing. The drawing is a translation hypothesis, not a vendor icon redraw.

The filter

A proposal earns space only if pyblocks could recognise a real Python semantic fact and the visual makes that fact clearer without giving the canvas a second program to maintain.

FramingTrack A · vocabularyTrack B · controlsSharpenedDecision surfaceSources
Conclusion

Borrow constraints, not palettes

The positive gaps are intentionally narrow: named partial updates, value selection, explicit outcomes, queue/event relations, a high-bar mode region, and source-derived interface exposure. The rest of the reference surface mostly belongs to authoring tools or host runtimes.

Why convergence matters: independent tools keep converging on visible joins, prior values, named fields, and explicit outcomes because dataflow puts hard constraints on an honest drawing. That is evidence for a source-derived presentation grammar—not permission to reproduce a LabVIEW, Blueprint, or Simulink library.

A · dictionary

Track A · node and block vocabulary

Concepts pyblocks might render as a block, region, port, or relation when source really carries the shape. Entries are organized by concept, not vendor.

Already have

Current SystemSketch UI is the proof; no hypothetical replacement drawing.

Concept and readingEvidence and SystemSketch projection
Already have
A-HAVE · 01

Exclusive branch / case / φ join

Python if and match already read as an exclusive Branch region with a join. LabVIEW Case, Blueprint Branch/Switch, and Simulink If/Merge confirm the settled reading grammar; they do not justify a new palette node.

Primary documentation: NI Case Structures · Epic Flow Control · MathWorks If

Existing SystemSketch UI
Already have
A-HAVE · 02

Loop-carried previous value / delayed edge

A loop-carried value already has a distinct z⁻¹ treatment, separating a prior iteration from same-iteration data. LabVIEW Feedback and Simulink Unit Delay corroborate that reading while their simulation-time rules remain outside ordinary Python.

Primary documentation: NI Feedback Node · MathWorks Unit Delay

Existing SystemSketch UI
Already have
A-HAVE · 03

Generic source ports and explicit receiver boundary

Calls, values, and explicit receivers already have a neutral block/port treatment, so a dataflow reader can follow a source expression without importing a foreign library palette. This is the existing foundation that a later named-field projection would refine—not a claim that every Python mapping is a static record.

Primary documentation: NI Unbundle By Name · Epic Struct Variables

Existing SystemSketch UI
Already have
A-HAVE · 04

Normal return versus derived mutation effect

A port declared mutating already derives a top-edge effect exit, preventing an in-place-looking write from reading like an ordinary returned value. This borrows the reader benefit of Blueprint pure/impure distinction without importing pervasive execution cables.

Primary documentation: Epic Functions

Concept and readingEvidence and SystemSketch projection
Missing, would be useful
A-USEFUL · 01

Named record-field projection

A reader should recognise a resolved record boundary and see name-stable members that really come from source: dataclass attributes, TypedDict keys, named-tuple fields, or well-resolved destructuring. The semantic is named field access, not a generic Struct node or an invented schema for dynamic mappings.

Primary documentation: NI Unbundle By Name · Epic Struct Variables · MathWorks Bus Selector

Official reference UI

Lift · medium to high. It needs record-identity and field-resolution facts, conservative fallbacks for dynamic attributes, and a compact group/port treatment that never lies about an unresolved mapping.

Missing, would be useful
A-USEFUL · 02

Named partial record update / portless effect endpoint

Bundle By Name, Set Members in Struct, and Bus Assignment all make a named partial update legible while leaving untouched fields intact. The Python translation is a source-recognized field write or batched setattr with an effect continuation—not an aggregate-update palette block.

Primary documentation: NI Bundle By Name · Epic Struct Variables · MathWorks Bus Assignment

Official reference UI

Lift · medium. The current top-edge effect port is a foundation. A portless endpoint needs a narrow analyzer fact, connection rules, and regression coverage for chained/batched writes.

Missing, would be useful
A-USEFUL · 03

Conditional value selection

LabVIEW Select and Simulink Switch make a value choice distinct from an effectful branch. Project only a Python conditional expression or value-producing match; do not copy Blueprint’s authoring-time addable option pins.

Primary documentation: NI Select · Epic Make Select · MathWorks Switch

Official reference UI

Lift · low to medium. The source shape is crisp, but it needs a decision about coexistence with the settled Branch region and the existing V4 Select candidate.

Missing, would be useful
A-USEFUL · 04

Explicit exception / non-normal outcome

LabVIEW error wiring and Blueprint Cast Failed both keep a non-normal route visible. Python should render only source-owned try/except/else/finally/raise or a separately proven narrowing boundary—not synthesize an error pin on every call.

Primary documentation: NI Handling Errors · Epic Cast To GameInstance

Official reference UI

Lift · medium to high. Needs an analyzer-owned boundary, nesting/re-raise rules, a region/rail grammar, and tests proving normal data never reads as an exception route.

Missing, would be useful
A-USEFUL · 05

Buffered async handoff / queue ownership

LabVIEW distinguishes asynchronous channel wires from synchronous wires, and Simulink makes function-call events explicit. The useful Python projection is a named handoff only for proof-quality asyncio.Queue, async/await, or an equivalent local producer/consumer source—not a fabricated global timeline.

Primary documentation: NI Using Wires · MathWorks Trigger · Epic Async

Official reference UI

Lift · high. Source recognition, cross-function identity, queue ownership wording, and a non-DAG layout contract must be designed before this can be honest.

Missing, would be useful
A-USEFUL · 06

Named event subscription / dispatch

LabVIEW user events, Blueprint dispatchers, and Stateflow event transitions make registration and delivery distinct from an ordinary value wire. Draw an event relation only when registration and emission resolve to a named Python callback/event-loop identity that a reader can trace to source.

Primary documentation: NI Event Structure · Epic Bind/Unbind · MathWorks Stateflow Events

Official reference UI

Lift · high. Start with one explicit idiom. Invisible observer relationships and framework callbacks the analyzer cannot resolve must remain undescribed.

Missing, would be useful
A-USEFUL · 07

Explicit mode / state-machine region

Stateflow’s states, transitions, and event labels are excellent prior art for a real mode model. A SystemSketch state region is justified only by an explicit analyzer-recognized state-machine protocol, never merely by an enum field or ordinary conditional chain.

Primary documentation: MathWorks Stateflow States · MathWorks Stateflow transitions

Official reference UI

Lift · very high. This is new semantic topology. Zach needs to choose the exact source contract first; a false-positive statechart would be worse than no statechart.

Missing, would not be useful

Text only by design: these would add palette or host-runtime semantics, not reveal Python.

Concept and readingEvidence and SystemSketch projection
Missing, would not be useful

Arithmetic, comparisons, collections, and signal-routing palettes

LabVIEW numeric/Boolean, Blueprint Array/Map/Set, and Simulink math/routing palettes are authoring conveniences. Python already states operators, calls, unpacking, indexing, and collection construction; special glyph libraries would add a second language rather than a renderer fact.

Missing, would not be useful

Sequence, Gate, DoOnce, Delay, timed loop, and scheduler controls

These encode tool-specific pulses, latches, wall-clock policy, or simulator scheduling. Preserve explicit Python order and draw a state/async relation only when source proves the underlying semantic contract.

Missing, would not be useful

Formula/MATLAB Function, macros, and authorable interface subgraphs

These are text escape hatches or reusable graph-authoring systems in palette tools. SystemSketch already takes the stronger source-first position: Python is canonical and linked definitions are the presentation seam.

Missing, would not be useful

Property/Invoke, variants, construction/spawn, hardware, and runtime palettes

Framework APIs, Unreal lifecycle nodes, LabVIEW hardware controls, and Simulink time/sample-rate configuration belong to their host runtimes. They are ordinary Python calls or deliberately outside a static Python renderer.

Missing, would not be useful

State history junctions and visual variant pickers

History restoration and variant activation have specialised runtime contracts but no dependable generic Python syntax. Do not infer hidden statechart memory or add a canvas-side configuration picker.

Track B · UI controls and presentation

Controls that change how an existing source-derived block reads. The question is always whether a control reveals a Python fact or imports an authoring/runtime surface.

Already have

Current SystemSketch UI is the proof; no hypothetical replacement drawing.

Concept and readingEvidence and SystemSketch projection
Already have
B-HAVE · 01

Simple / Port / Expanded presentation

Compactness is already reversible presentation: Simple, Port, and Expanded views change density without deleting source-derived relationships. LabVIEW icon view, Blueprint collapsed graphs, and Simulink subsystems are convergence evidence, not a license for new nested graph semantics.

Primary documentation: NI View As Icon · Epic Collapsing Graphs · MathWorks Subsystem

B-HAVE · 02

Manual port visibility and row placement

A port can already live in a header row, body row, or hidden state. This is the useful analogue of Blueprint As Pin and source-derived subsystem placement because it changes readability without changing Python’s callable interface.

Primary documentation: Epic Struct Variables · MathWorks Connect Subsystems

An unwired parameter can already show its literal value directly on the port, making a default legible rather than missing. That is a presentation fact that aligns with terminal/pin defaults in the reference tools.

The inspector mirrors selected block/port presentation state, including visibility and defaults. It is a canvas presentation editor—not Blueprint asset authoring or Simulink mask programming.

B-USEFUL · 01

Source-derived required/defaulted/keyword-only call contract

LabVIEW terminal categories and generated Blueprint/Simulink function pins make an interface scanable. Render factual Python distinctions—required, defaulted, keyword-only, and later variadic—without importing LabVIEW cable legality or an invented recommended category.

Primary documentation: NI terminal categories · Epic Functions · MathWorks Function Caller

Official reference UI

Lift · medium. It needs signature facts from the analyzer and a density-tested badge hierarchy, but no new language semantics or canvas-authorable ports.

Missing, would be useful
B-USEFUL · 02

Default provenance and override visibility

A call site should distinguish a source signature default, a literal supplied at the call, and a connected upstream value. The current literal pill is the right local primitive; source-derived provenance would make the resolved call contract legible without ever mutating the canonical default from the board.

Primary documentation: NI terminal categories · Epic Functions

Official reference UI

Lift · medium. It shares call-resolution facts with the contract display and should be designed alongside it, but can remain deferred if the compact view becomes visually dense.

Missing, would be useful
B-USEFUL · 03

Source-derived record member exposure

Blueprint exposes selected struct fields as pins while LabVIEW and Simulink select named aggregate elements. Keep the existing manual visibility baseline, then suggest only knowable dataclass/TypedDict/record fields; readers may collapse a field but cannot manufacture a schema.

Primary documentation: NI Unbundle By Name · Epic Struct Variables · MathWorks Bus Selector

Official reference UI

Lift · medium. Needs safe field discovery and a compact expand/collapse interaction. Unknown attributes, dynamic mappings, and framework magic remain ordinary source expressions.

Missing, would be useful
B-USEFUL · 04

Source-derived variadic parameter summary

Blueprint Add Pin controls exist because Blueprint authors node interfaces. Python variadics already exist in source as *args and **kwargs; an expandable summary can reveal that fact without allowing the canvas to alter a signature.

Primary documentation: Epic Add Pin interface · Epic Functions

Official reference UI

Lift · low to medium. Follow call-contract work once the analyzer publishes variadic facts. The interaction must be a presentation expansion, never a plus/minus pin editor.

Missing, would be useful
B-USEFUL · 05

Generated, source-linked configuration lens

Simulink masks and Blueprint Details panels show why readers sometimes need an interface-oriented configuration view. The useful translation is a generated, read-only source lens for constructor/function defaults and annotations—not an author-defined dialog or callback surface.

Primary documentation: MathWorks Dynamic Mask Dialog · Epic Functions

Official reference UI

Lift · medium to high. Useful only after a clear source link and read-only boundary. It belongs beside the inspector, not in a programmable mask system.

Missing, would be useful
B-USEFUL · 06

Semantic relation inspection

When a future outcome, queue, event, or state relation is recognised, line styling alone cannot explain its proof boundary. A read-only inspector should state the source pattern, known endpoints, and the limitations it deliberately does not claim—such as ordering or cancellation.

Primary documentation: NI Event Structure · Epic Bind/Unbind · MathWorks Stateflow Events

Official reference UI

Lift · medium after Track A. This is not standalone UI work: build it only once the corresponding semantic relation already has a source-recognised visual grammar.

Concept and readingEvidence and SystemSketch projection
Missing, would not be useful

Author-defined masks, callbacks, and custom block faces

Simulink masks let a block author program dialogs, callbacks, icons, and port presentation. That is a second UI/programming surface and reverses Python-source authority, so it is not a SystemSketch control.

Missing, would not be useful

LabVIEW recommended wiring legality

Python has required and defaulted arguments but no semantic equivalent of a recommended terminal. A third visual tier that changes cable validity would state a false contract.

Missing, would not be useful

Automatic wire-driven hiding and user-authored advanced-pin metadata

Blueprint can hide unconnected pins and use metadata to expose advanced fields. Letting current wiring determine a source signature’s visible truth would be misleading; retain explicit presentation controls and derive only analyzer-known facts.

Missing, would not be useful

Drag-created or repositioned source interface ports

Simulink authors may create, rename, and move subsystem ports; Blueprint authoring nodes add pins. SystemSketch may change display placement, but source owns whether a callable port exists, so a canvas gesture cannot create the interface.

Missing, would not be useful

Host-runtime property sheets and review-thread lifecycle

LabVIEW Property/Invoke, Unreal asset Details, and Simulink resolved-review workflows are host/application behavior. The generic inspector and anchored comments are sufficient renderer-side seams; framework-specific property UI is not.

Synthesis

Your thinking, sharpened

These are deliberately scoped inferences from the cited documentation and the current tree—not claims that the tools share an execution model.

1 · The error wire’s lesson is visible outcome, not plumbing.

Python’s honest translation is a source-aware exception/narrowing boundary, never a red pin placed on every ordinary call.

2 · Async needs identity, not only a dash pattern.

The existing style becomes semantic only when the analyzer can name a queue, await, registration, or callback contract.

3 · Named fields converge because identity matters.

Unbundle By Name, struct pins, and bus selection preserve named-member identity rather than positional coincidence.

4 · Python has a cleaner interface vocabulary.

Required/defaulted/keyword-only/variadic is more truthful than LabVIEW’s recommended wiring tier and does not make a cable legal or illegal.

5 · State is a semantic commitment.

Stateflow is compelling because the chart owns a true state model. An inferred statechart for ordinary enum-and-if code would mislead.

6 · Parameter dialogs divide at authority.

A generated source lens could help a reader; an authorable mask or callback system would create another program on the canvas.

Decision surface

No product code changes are hidden in this research artifact. Useful entries are staged options, not implementation commitments.

Done

  • Rebuilt the report as two extensive concept dictionaries.
  • Captured and embedded 23 primary-source reference images.
  • Used actual SystemSketch UI captures for every shipped entry.

Left

  • Choose one exception/narrowing shape and one async/event idiom before analyzer work.
  • Define safe record-field discovery and a small portless-effect experiment.
  • Prototype signature density only after analyzer facts exist.

Needs Zach

  • Which first outcome syntax deserves projection?
  • Which async relation is worth drawing first?
  • What source contract, if any, earns a state region?
  • Should a source lens follow call-contract work?

Deliberately not done

  • No draggable vendor-style palette.
  • No universal error wire, global timeline, inferred statechart, or user-authored schema.
  • No mask/dialog programming or host-runtime property UI.
  • No SystemSketch product/schema/analyzer change.
